quote: Example 3. Consider Y1 and Y2 with cdfs G1(y) = y/β1 (0 ≤ y ≤ β1) and G2(y) = y/β2 (0 ≤ y ≤ β2), respectively. For β2 ≥ β1, Y1 ≤sto Y2 holds. Applying Table 1, we compute RFGxΦν(Y1) = β1 κ(ν)/(ν + 1) ≤ β2 κ(ν)/(ν + 1) = RFGxΦν(Y2).
family: Uniform on (0, β): G(y) = y/β; parameters β1, β2 > 0
quantifiers: all y; ν ≥ 1 for the extropy comparison
numbers: RFGxΦν(Y1) = β1 κ(ν)/(ν+1) ≤ β2 κ(ν)/(ν+1) = RFGxΦν(Y2), supporting Theorem 6
ambiguity: Text layer garbles the cdf fractions ('G1(y) = β y'); reconstructed as y/β1, uniform on (0,β1), consistent with Table 1's uniform row.

quote: Corollary 1. 1. Assume that Y(k) and Z(K) denote the Kth order statistic from samples Y1, Y2, . . . , Ys and Z1, Z2, . . . , Zs, respectively, both of size s. If Y ≤sto Z, then Y(k) ≤sto Z(k), which implies RFGxΦν(Y(k)) ≥ RFGxΦν(Z(k)) for all k = 1, 2, . . . , s, ν ≥ 1.
family: i.i.d. samples from arbitrary nonnegative distributions Y and Z
compared: parent distributions Y vs Z; same sample size s and same rank k
